northwest-hills: Northwest Hills is one of Austin's most established and sought-after neighborhoods, set in the rolling, tree-covered hills west of MoPac and north of RM 2222. Most homes were built from the 1960s through the 1980s on generous, wooded lots, and many of the higher streets enjoy Hill Country views.

Day-to-day life here is easy. Far West Boulevard is lined with neighborhood restaurants, coffee shops and grocery stores, and the Arboretum and the Domain are a short drive north. Getting outside comes naturally, with Bull Creek Park and its greenbelt, Northwest District Park and Mount Bonnell all close by.

Northwest Hills is served by Austin ISD, including Doss and Hill Elementary, Murchison Middle School and Anderson High School (assignments vary by street). With quick access to MoPac and Loop 360, downtown is about 15 minutes away, and the major tech employers of north and northwest Austin are an easy commute.

westover-hills: Westover Hills is an upscale, well-established, family-friendly neighborhood in Northwest Austin, just north of Far West Boulevard. Its roughly 1,500 single-family homes were built mostly from 1965 through 1978, many on large lots with tall, mature trees and beautifully landscaped yards.

The streets are quiet and ideal for an early-morning or evening jog, yet you're close to everything. Downtown Austin is under nine miles away, the Arboretum is just across Loop 360, and the shopping and dining at the Domain are minutes north. Excellent health care, greenbelt trails and plenty of outdoor recreation are nearby, along with quick access to MoPac, Loop 360 and US 183.

Westover Hills is served by Austin ISD schools, including Hill Elementary, Murchison Middle School and Anderson High School (assignments vary by street), and it offers a short commute to the major tech employers of north and northwest Austin.
